certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Food and Agriculture / Foodgrain Products and Starches)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Certification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Starch manufacturers can apply for a license to use the prestigious BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on product containers to convey quality assurance. Additionally, product marking, net weight declarations, and labeling must satisfy statutory food safety standards, including the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations.

requirements.detail: The method of drawing representative samples of arrowroot starch must conform to the requirements and sample-extraction procedures specified in IS 4662-1977.
Starch content and moisture content must be tested separately on each of the individual samples drawn from the lot.
All remaining physical, chemical, and microscopic requirements (such as ash, acid insoluble ash, pH, or particle size) must be tested on a unified composite sample.

The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of the specification if and only if all the test results obtained from both the individual samples and the composite sample satisfy the relevant specification limits.

To determine compliance with the chemical, moisture, or particulate limits of this standard, the final observed or calculated value of any test or analysis must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded value must match the specified limit in this standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1006 : 1984 (Second Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements, sampling plans, and testing methods for arrowroot starch, popularly known as 'arrowroot'. Formulated under the Foodgrains, Allied Products and Ready-to-Eat Foods Sectional Committee (FAD 16) and reaffirmed in 2022, this standard ensures the purity, safety, and consistency of arrowroot starch extracted from the rhizomes of Maranta arundinacea. It mandates specific sampling under IS 4662, dictates that moisture and starch content must be analyzed on each individual sample while other parameters are checked on a composite sample, and enforces strict mathematical rounding protocols under IS 2:1960 to verify conformity.
